target_customer: Banks, credit unions and private lenders that administer construction loans, plus real estate developers and asset managers
problem: Construction loan draws are processed manually from budgets, invoices and lien releases, which is slow and error-prone.
business_model: B2B SaaS for lenders and developers

founders.name: Will Mitchell
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a commercial real estate background without detail.

technical_complexity.rationale: Document extraction and reconciliation of budgets, pay applications and invoices, with later machine learning, is standard engineering with some hard data-quality parts.

defensibility.rationale: Lenders embed draw workflows and loan data, and lender-specific document rules create stickiness. Larger construction software suites could still add the feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source dated to the time was found. Today's comparison blogs put Textura (payments) and Procore (project management) in the broader market, and no acquisition of Rabbet was found.

market_need_then: Construction lenders ran draws by hand. A 2019 article describes Rabbet linking budget, pay application, invoice and lien release data. No 2017 evidence of demand was opened.

branding.domain_note: Uses the exact rabbet.com domain per the YC page. The company was formerly Contract Simply.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise B2B with a woodworking-themed quote about strengthening joints in one article

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources found. Built In reported the Series A following the rebrand.

brand_strength.rationale: A rabbet is a woodworking joint, a real word that suits construction, and the rebrand from a generic name gave a more distinctive brand. No evidence beyond that.

outcome_analysis: Rabbet raised a seed in October 2017 and an $8M Series A in February 2019 backed by Goldman Sachs, QED and Camber Creek, then grew with bank and servicer customers such as Berkadia in 2023. No acquisition or layoffs were found. Capital raised is modest, so success is judged by customer logos rather than later rounds.
notes: Series A was confirmed by several outlets, one of which says QED led. The seed lead Tectonic Capital comes from one article. YC page names only Will Mitchell. The company site says Austin, YC says Denver. No dated competitor sources were found, so the list is empty.
